segments.t: Out by the van, Timur defends his zombie-bitten nephew on grounds of family honor, and when a groaning Chef Barinov stumbles out, Louis mistakes his hangover for the zombie virus.
Ты чего, это же мой племянник!
Если он укусит, вы станете зомби!
У нас укусить старшего — это позор.
Тогда мы с вами никуда не поедем.
Ох, мои бедные мозги!
Давай садись в машину уже.
О ужас, что я наделал!
У меня просто не было выбора.
Наш шеф тоже стал зомби!
Какой ещё зомби, идиоты?
У меня с утра дикое похмелье!
Я всю ночь Кровавую Мэри пил!
А вы орёте так, что мозги болят!
Let's walk through each line of the comedy in the courtyard.
Ты чего, это же мой племянник!

'What are you doing, that is my nephew!' Because what are Barinov doing that is his nephew, Timur does not bother softening the blow for Barinov. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
Если он укусит, вы станете зомби!

'If he bites you, you will become a zombie!' Insisting that if he bites Barinov Barinov will become a zombie shows Louis is not backing down. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
У нас укусить старшего — это позор.
'Where we come from, biting an elder is a disgrace.' Mentioning that where they come from biting an elder is a disgrace moves the talk in a new direction.
Тогда мы с вами никуда не поедем.

'Then we are not driving anywhere with you.' Saying that they are not driving anywhere with Barinov is how Louis sets the tone with Barinov. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
Ох, мои бедные мозги!
'Oh, my poor brains!' Over the shift and the respect, Barinov lets his real feelings show. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.
Давай садись в машину уже.
'Come on, get into the car already.' Once Barinov should come on get into the car already, Timur can finally tell Barinov what he means.
О ужас, что я наделал!
'Oh horror, what have I done!' Louis declares that horror what have he done as the tension in the room peaks. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.
У меня просто не было выбора.

'I simply had no choice.' Claiming that he simply had no choice sounds confident, even if Barinov has doubts. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
Наш шеф тоже стал зомби!
'Our chef has become a zombie too!' Insisting that their has become a zombie shows Louis is not backing down.
Какой ещё зомби, идиоты?

'What zombie, you idiots?' Over the moment and the respect, Barinov presses Louis for a straight answer. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
У меня с утра дикое похмелье!

'I have a wild hangover this morning!' Having a wild hangover this morning is Barinov's blunt reaction in front of Louis. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
Я всю ночь Кровавую Мэри пил!
'I was drinking Bloody Marys all night!' Barinov insists that he was drinking all night, leaving Louis no room to argue.
А вы орёте так, что мозги болят!

'And you are yelling so loud that my brains hurt!' Saying that Louis is yelling so loud that his brains hurt is how Barinov takes charge of the moment. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects. Now let's hear the whole scene again from start to finish.
Ты чего, это же мой племянник!
Если он укусит, вы станете зомби!
У нас укусить старшего — это позор.
Тогда мы с вами никуда не поедем.
Ох, мои бедные мозги!
Давай садись в машину уже.
О ужас, что я наделал!
У меня просто не было выбора.
Наш шеф тоже стал зомби!
Какой ещё зомби, идиоты?
У меня с утра дикое похмелье!
Я всю ночь Кровавую Мэри пил!
А вы орёте так, что мозги болят!
Listen for the verb 'nadelat' in Louis's cry 'What have I done!' — adding the prefix 'na-' implies doing something bad or making a big mess. See you next time!
Хорошего дня!
